taxpayer.notes: Filed Form 1040A; standard deduction $9,250 claimed (filing status not stated). Pro se. All amounts rounded to nearest dollar per opinion.

notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Claims gambling losses exceeding winnings; claims $6,500 IRA deduction
conceded: Petitioner admits $2,994 gambling winnings (but claims offsetting losses)

findings_of_fact.fact: 2015 salary from State of Arizona $28,577; W-2 wages $25,687
findings_of_fact.snippet: paid a salary of $28,577, of which $25,687 was reported as wages on petitioner's 2015 Form W-2

findings_of_fact.fact: $2,890 contributed to Arizona State Retirement System excluded from W-2 wages (pretax)
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner's Form W-2 did not include $2,890 that he contributed to the Arizona State Retirement System for 2015.
reported income of $25,687 from wages and claimed a deduction of $6,500 for an IRA contribution

findings_of_fact.fact: Two Forms W-2G totaling $2,994 gambling winnings; no records kept
findings_of_fact.snippet: in the total amount of $2,994. Petitioner did not maintain records of his gambling activity
petitioner received $25 of interest income during 2015

findings_of_fact.fact: Standard deduction $9,250 claimed; no itemized deductions
findings_of_fact.snippet: chose to use the standard deduction of $9,250

findings_of_fact.fact: Would need more than $6,256 of additional itemized deductions beyond $2,994 losses to exceed the standard deduction
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner would have to come up with more than $6,256 of additional itemized deductions

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner computed $6,500 roughly by doubling his $2,890 contribution
findings_of_fact.snippet: by doubling his $2,890 contribution to the Arizona State Retirement System

issues.question: Must petitioner include $25 of unreported interest income for 2015?
issues.holding: Yes; petitioner admitted the interest income
issues.computable_reason: Admitted receipt; inclusion follows mechanically from §61

issues.question: Must petitioner include $2,994 of W-2G gambling winnings, and can unsubstantiated gambling losses offset them?
issues.holding: Winnings includible; no records of losses, and even if $2,994 losses substantiated, as itemized deductions they would not exceed the $9,250 standard deduction
issues.computable_reason: Alternative ground is pure arithmetic: losses capped at winnings ($2,994) as itemized deduction < $9,250 standard deduction (substantiation failure also noted)

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to a $6,500 IRA deduction based on pretax contributions to the Arizona State Retirement System?
issues.holding: No; the $2,890 contribution was a pretax reduction of wages and pretax contributions are not deductible
issues.computable_reason: Contribution already excluded from wages; no deductible IRA contribution exists on found facts

decision.text: Decision will be entered for respondent.
decision.summary: $1,907 deficiency sustained: interest and gambling winnings included; IRA deduction disallowed

notes: No penalties determined. Filing status not stated. Gambling-loss holding rests on both lack of records and standard-deduction arithmetic (derived: 9,250 - 2,994 = 6,256).
